findings.claim: _targets stripped .okf/ before checking for docs/, so .okf/docs/how-to/run.md was accepted and wrote docs/how-to/run.md

verdict.text: An id that starts with `.okf/` now always resolves under `.okf/`, so `.okf/docs/how-to/run.md` is refused and no file changes.
The nearby spellings still work, and the r4 test now covers this case.
Gates: I re-ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
Lint, tests, integration and rows r1 to r6 all passed: "stamp green: f6558b8d9250678e12e282d4b8d86564c2bbc0e29cb9d6000fb07246583fbd75".
`in_okf` is set before the prefix is stripped, and `docs` now requires `not in_okf`.
Base, shown path, canonical id and the `_pages` set then all point at `.okf/`.
The canonical check still compares against the stripped id, so `.okf/decisions/0001-a.md` stays accepted.
A real `docs/how-to/run.md` is present in its fixture, and the test asserts exit 1, one refusal line on stderr, and no file changed.
Probes in a scratch repo with `--by human:t`: `.okf/docs/how-to/run.md` was refused with "no concept, docs page or folder ... at .okf/docs/how-to/run(.md)", and the tree stayed clean.
`docs/how-to/run`, `docs/how-to/run.md` and `.okf/decisions/0001-a.md` each still verified the right file.
`packages/kmctl/src/kmctl/verify.py:107-109` (the `in_okf` flag) fixes it, and the r4 parametrized case covers it.
